parent: reLink Medical, LLC (independent, Dalton family owned; president and CEO Jeff Dalton)
notes: ScripType reported in January 2019 that reLink Medical moved 43 employees from Aurora to 1755 Enterprise Parkway in Twinsburg and expected more than 60 within eighteen months, quoting president and CEO Jeff Dalton, who had earlier started and sold PartsSource. The company's own site still gives that Twinsburg address as its headquarters and names no parent, so the 2021-2022 grant years fall in the 60 to 120 range, consistent with JobsOhio's 28 jobs retained.

company: CIC Group, Inc. (via Nooter Construction Company)
parent: CIC Group, Inc. (1509 Ocello Dr., St. Louis, Missouri)
notes: Nooter's own history page shows that Nooter bought RMF Industrial Contracting in 2003 to form RMF Nooter LLC and rebranded it under the single Nooter name in 2020, and the site is published under cicgroup.com with CIC Group Inc. of St. Louis as the copyright holder. Nooter Construction alone runs offices in St. Louis, Philadelphia, Toledo, Chicago, Los Angeles, Atlanta and Boston, and CIC Group holds five such operating companies, so the group is well above 500 worldwide; no company page states an exact headcount.

parent: London Computer Systems, Inc. (founder-owned; president and CEO Dave Hegemann)
notes: The company's own About page names Dave Hegemann as founder, president and CEO and places the headquarters on Waterstone Boulevard in Cincinnati, with no parent or outside owner mentioned. Form 5500 participants rose from 255 in 2019 to 437 in 2023, and JobsOhio counted 177 jobs retained, which puts the 2020-2021 grant years in the 300-400 range and below the 500 line.

company: Vigilant, LLC dba Vigilant Technology Solutions
parent: Vigilant, LLC (independent; no parent named on the company site)
notes: Vigilant's own site gives its global headquarters as 7723 Tylers Place Blvd., Suite 181, West Chester, Ohio, with remote operations in Lexington, Kentucky and no parent or group named anywhere on the site. Form 5500 showed 20 participants in 2019 and directories list about 40, so the company stayed far below 500 through the 2022-2024 grant years; no source publishes a current headcount.

parent: S&P Data Digital (2 Bloor Street W, Suite 2005, Toronto, Ontario, Canada; co-founder and CEO Dan Plashkes)
notes: The group's current site gives its head office as 2 Bloor Street West in Toronto and names Dan Plashkes as CEO and co-founder, with no U.S. parent. Cleveland.com reported that the S&P Data call center tripled its downtown Cleveland space and expected to add 325 jobs in twelve months, so the Ohio site alone approached 400 and the contact-center group across Canada and the United States was well above 500 in the 2018 and 2021 grant years; no company page publishes a worldwide headcount.

parent: Taiho Kogyo Co., Ltd. (3-65 Midorigaoka, Toyota City, Aichi, Japan; Tokyo Stock Exchange Standard Market, code 6470)
notes: Taiho Kogyo's own overseas-subsidiary page lists Taiho Corporation of America at 194 Heritage Drive, Tiffin, Ohio 44883, the grantee's address, and its company outline reports 4,089 consolidated employees against 1,885 at the parent alone. The Tiffin plant is the U.S. arm of a listed Japanese group, so the size and home state follow the parent.

parent: StandardAero, Inc. (Scottsdale, Arizona; majority-owned by Carlyle Group funds during the grant years, publicly traded as NYSE: SARO since October 2024)
notes: The Cincinnati grantee, StandardAero Component Services, is a unit of StandardAero, Inc., whose 10-K reports about 7,700 employees worldwide at the end of 2024 and about 7,300 at the end of 2023, and whose business address is 6710 North Scottsdale Road, Scottsdale, Arizona. Carlyle held majority ownership across the 2017, 2021 and 2022 grant years, and a private-equity fund is not counted as the parent, so the parent is StandardAero itself.

parent: Bright Innovation Labs (formerly Bright International, founded 1987 by Anthony Bibars; owned by Aterian Investment Partners funds since August 2019), corporate headquarters Santa Clarita, California in the grant year
notes: Private Equity Professional reported in February 2021 that Aterian-backed Bright International bought Bocchi Laboratories, the New Albany grantee's owner, from the Bocchi family, and an archived November 2021 capture of brightinnovationlabs.com names Santa Clarita, California as the corporate headquarters, with plants of 225,000 square feet in California, 200,000 in Ohio and 122,000 in Arizona. Aterian is a private-equity fund, so the parent is the Bright operating group; no source publishes a headcount, so Large rests on the scale of three high-volume filling plants, against a 100-participant Form 5500 at the Ohio sponsor.

company: FEW Automotive Glass Applications Group (Zwenkau, Germany)
parent: FEW Fahrzeugelektrik Werk GmbH & Co. KG (FEW Automotive Group), Polierweg 6, 04442 Zwenkau, Germany

KG, founded 1995, with its head office and all central functions in Zwenkau, Germany, plus production in Shanghai and a U.S. operation that grew out of a 2009 sales representation and a 2011 automated line. parent: Mucci Farms (Mucci International Marketing Inc.), Kingsville, Ontario, Canada

parent: Selman & Company, LLC (privately held; David L. Selman, managing director)
notes: SelmanCo's own site says it is one of the largest privately held U.S. life and supplemental health insurance administration firms and that its workforce of 200 professionals is headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio at One Integrity Parkway, the Richmond Heights address on the grant record, with offices in Keene, New Hampshire and Baltimore.
